senses.definition: A rule for what a scheduler does when a job's planned start time was missed.
senses.caution: Used with schedulers such as Quartz or APScheduler. It covers runs that were skipped, not runs that started and then failed.
senses.example: Our misfire policy runs a missed job once as soon as the scheduler is back and skips the rest.

cues.text: The scheduler was down over a weekend and missed three nightly jobs. You configure whether to run them all on restart, run one, or skip them, and you need the name of that setting.
A design doc asks what happens when a job's planned time passes while the system is paused. You name the rule you have to define.
A reviewer asks whether a report due at midnight should run late or be dropped if the cluster was down at that moment. You want the term for the setting that decides.

distractors: A rule for how many times a failed request is sent again before the system finally gives up on it.
A limit on how many jobs can run at the same moment on one machine before others must wait.
A schedule that starts a job at the same hour every day.
A message sent to the team when a job fails.
A record of every change made to a job.
